recent_posts.title: Apache Geode 2.0, Part II: Rebuilding a Distributed System for the Modern Java Era
recent_posts.summary: Apache Geode 2.0 underwent a major modernization effort, migrating from JDK 8 to JDK 17, adopting Jakarta EE 10, upgrading to Spring Framework 6, and rewriting the CLI with Spring Shell 3.x. The upgrade followed a strict dependency order to avoid cascading failures across 11,000+ Java classes and 32 subprojects. Security was a primary driver, addressing deserialization flaws, SSRF risks, and authentication weaknesses. The effort resulted in 800+ changed files, 18,000+ lines added, and all 10,600+ tests passing. Breaking changes include dropping support for legacy Tomcat versions 6–9.

recent_posts.title: The Public CA clientAuth EKU Sunset: What Apache Software Deployers Need to Know
recent_posts.summary: Starting May 2026, major public Certificate Authorities (CAs) including Let's Encrypt, DigiCert, Sectigo, and GlobalSign will stop including the Client Authentication Extended Key Usage (EKU) in publicly issued TLS certificates. This affects any deployment using mutual TLS (mTLS) with public-CA-issued client certificates — including Apache Kafka, Cassandra, ZooKeeper, Pulsar, Ignite, and Geode. Failures won't appear immediately but will surface silently during routine certificate renewals, potentially causing cascading authentication failures in distributed systems. Three migration paths are outlined: switching to an internal/enterprise CA for all certificates, using a hybrid model (public CA for servers, private CA for clients), or moving to server-only TLS with application-layer authentication. Deployers should immediately audit their environments, identify affected certificates using OpenSSL or keytool commands, and begin migration planning before the deadline.

recent_posts.title: ASF Plus One Newsletter: April 2026
recent_posts.summary: The Apache Software Foundation's April 2026 Plus One newsletter covers community highlights including a new 'Plus One People' blog series featuring ASF board member Jean-Baptiste Onofré, mentorship success at OpenSource4You in Taiwan, and open registration for Community Over Code Glasgow 2026 (early-bird $500 until July 28). The ASF welcomed 45 new members bringing total membership to 1,188. A major Responsible AI Initiative has launched with $1.75M in initial funding from Anthropic ($1.5M) and Alpha-Omega ($250K), targeting $10M total to strengthen open source AI infrastructure. The newsletter also warns of phishing attempts in community Slack workspaces and notes 53 ASF projects made 252 releases in the past month.

recent_posts.title: Lessons from Log4Shell: Building a CRA-Ready Log4j
recent_posts.summary: The VP of Logging at the Apache Software Foundation recounts how the Log4Shell vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228) forced a comprehensive overhaul of the Log4j project, and how that work aligns with the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). Key improvements include: rewriting documentation to surface security best practices and an explicit security model; migrating from manual builds to reproducible GitHub Actions CI with SLSA attestations; publishing CycloneDX SBOMs and developing automated VEX statements; establishing a structured vulnerability handling process including a bug bounty program; and modularizing Log4j 3 to reduce attack surface. The post also addresses the unsolved problem of maintainer sustainability, with only two active maintainers currently, and outlines community and funding initiatives to address it. The core message is that CRA compliance and a healthier open source project are the same goal.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Daniel Ruggeri as Executive Vice President of the Apache Software Foundation
recent_posts.summary: The Apache Software Foundation (ASF) has appointed Daniel Ruggeri as its new Executive Vice President. Ruggeri's involvement with the ASF began when he submitted a patch to the Apache HTTP Server while working as a server administrator at Mastercard. He later became a committer, presented at ApacheCon, and served on the ASF board from 2019 to 2021. In his EVP role, he plans to focus on servant leadership and operational excellence, leveraging his background in web and cloud infrastructure, large team management, and budget oversight.

recent_posts.title: The Apache Software Foundation Welcomes 44 New Members
recent_posts.summary: The Apache Software Foundation (ASF) has elected 44 new members during its annual Members Meeting on March 5, 2026, bringing the total membership count to 1,187. New members are nominated by existing members from the pool of committers who have demonstrated merit in the Foundation's growth. Members play a governance role similar to shareholders, participating in Board and Member elections and helping ensure ASF projects follow The Apache Way.

recent_posts.title: The Apache Software Foundation Launches $10M Responsible AI Initiative with Initial $1.75M Donation
recent_posts.summary: The Apache Software Foundation has launched a Responsible AI Initiative with a $10 million funding goal, seeded by a $1.5 million donation from Anthropic and $250,000 from Alpha-Omega. The initiative aims to strengthen open source infrastructure underpinning modern AI systems over at least three years. It will provide ASF projects with access to AI models and tooling, ecosystem support for AI/ML development, and expanded community engagement opportunities including events and scholarships. The ASF also introduced guidelines for responsible AI use within its projects, emphasizing human oversight, licensing integrity, and security.

recent_posts.title: The Apache Software Foundation Announces $1.5M Donation from Anthropic
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic has donated $1.5 million to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) to support its infrastructure, security, and community operations. The donation will fund build systems, security processes, project services, and community support for Apache's hundreds of open source projects. Anthropic's CISO framed the contribution as a direct investment in the resilience of the open source systems that modern AI depends on. ASF President Ruth Suehle emphasized that reliable open source infrastructure requires sustained investment from across the ecosystem.

recent_posts.title: Breathing New Life into Apache Mahout: The Next Generation of Contributors
recent_posts.summary: A group of Taiwanese university students, mentored through the ALC Taipei (OpenSource4You) community, revitalized Apache Mahout by introducing the Quantum Data Plane (QDP) framework that bridges GPU and quantum computing. Starting from a single student's first patch, the effort grew into a team of committers and PMC members, produced academic papers, and is now preparing to mentor the next generation through GSoC 2026. The story highlights how community mentorship and 'The Apache Way' philosophy enabled young contributors to make a global impact on a dormant open source project.

recent_posts.title: Plus One People Series: JB Onofré
recent_posts.summary: Jean-Baptiste Onofré (JB), an ASF Board member and contributor to dozens of Apache projects, shares his open source journey starting in 2004, his current focus on big data projects like Apache Iceberg, Polaris, Arrow, and Beam, and his views on the future of open source. He discusses the rise of agentic AI, the EU Cyber Resilience Act's impact on security practices, and why the Apache Way's 'community over code' principle is critical for project sustainability. He also offers practical advice for newcomers looking to contribute to Apache projects.
